Home

Welcome
Visitors to our school frequently comment on the warm and nurturing feel they experience as soon as they walk through the door. Like me, our children are extremely proud of our school and this is shown in the caring and respectful way they interact with each other and their environment.
The educational experience at Shinfield St Mary’s is transformational. Based on our Christian vision of ‘‘As I have loved you, so you must love one another.’ John 13, 34 we teach far more than will be found in the National Curriculum. With love at the centre, our broad, inclusive and ambitious curriculum offers opportunities for all, while outstanding facilities and an array of community partnerships provide an abundance of extra-curricular activities – we provide a truly holistic education.
We were delighted to join the Agape Multi-Academy Trust on the 2nd February 2026. Information about the Trust can be found under the 'Our School' heading.

pageCache.text:
Our Governors
Local Governing Committee
On 1st February 2026 we joined the Agape Multi-Academy Trust (MAT). Each school within the Agape MAT has its own Local Governing Committee whose role and responsibilities are set out in a scheme of delegation.
If you wish to contact the Local Governing Committee, please email the Governance Professional clerk@shinfield-st-marys.wokingham.sch.uk
Members of the Local Governing Committee
Mrs Philippa Healy - Ex- Officio by virtue of office as Headteacher - Headteacher Shinfield St Marys - Term 24/4/2021
Mrs Jessica Dye - Chair of the Local Governing Committee and Lead Governor for Looked-After Children and Pupil Premium - Appointed by the Trust Board with the consent of the Oxford Diocesan Board of Education. Term 1/2/2026 - 31/2/2030
Miss Jackie Rance – Lead Governor for Access and Inclusion and Racial Equality - Appointed by the Trust with the consent of the Oxford Diocese Board of Education – Term - 12/3/2024 -11/3/2028
I am proud to be a Shinfield St. Marys Foundation Governor. All three of my grandsons have attended this school and loved their years here. My working background is the owner of a small cleaning business for over 25 years, being a Berkshire Magistrate working in Adult Criminal and Family Courts for 15 years, and I am currently a Shinfield Borough and Parish Councillor.
Mr Neil Manthey – Data/IT Link Governor - Parent Governor - Term 10/10/2023 – 9/10/2027
Neil Manthey is a School Governor with a strong personal connection to the school, having had two children progress through the school. He is keen to support the school community by bringing a parent’s perspective alongside professional experience in IT support and problem‑solving within a large organisation.
Neil has a particular interest in ensuring pupils are supported to achieve their full potential in a safe, inclusive, and well‑resourced environment. As a governor, he aims to provide constructive challenge, support school leadership, and help ensure decisions are made in the best interests of both students and staff.
Reverend Nigel Beer - Lead Governor for RE and Collective Worship - Appointed by the Trust with the consent of the Oxford Diocese Board of Education – term – 1/2/2026 - 31/1/2030
Nigel is the ordained Team Rector of the four parishes of the Loddon Reach Benefice which includes St Mary's, Shinfield. He is a regular visitor to the school involved in Collective Worship as well as governor visits and is delighted in seeing the growth in the positive link between the school and St Mary's Church. He has a particular interest in maintaining the distinctive Christian ethos of the school.
Mrs Beth Webster – Staff Governor – term 3/3/2025 – 2/3/2029
Role within school – Acting SENCO since 2024
For the past 30 years, I have been involved in working with children who have additional needs. I started my career by co-owning a Nursery school, spending some time as a TA in a mainstream Secondary school, then moving on to Further Education where I qualified as a Teacher in the FE sector. Most of my teaching was spent in the LLD/D (Learners with Learning Difficulties/and or Disabilities) department. I then became Special Education Manager for the College, securing funding, for and building a specialist ASD centre, which enabled the college to offer provision to students who would have normally been placed out of county. Following this, I moved on to become Group Learning Support Manager for Berkshire, overseeing in excess of 500 students with EHCP’s and ensuring that their needs were met during their time at College. After a short break, thinking that I wanted to retire, it soon became evident that I didn’t!
I have two daughters, and two stepchildren. Also 4 beautiful grandchildren, one of whom has ASD.
I absolutely love working at Shinfield St-Marys Junior School and am privileged to be doing a job that I am passionate about. Advocating for children with additional needs and ensuring that they are able to succeed and have the best education possible is of great importance to me. I have excellent relationships with our external service providers and aim to secure the best outcomes for both the children and the School.
I became a School Governor as I believe in being ‘present’ and contributing to strategic decisions which affect both the school and its staff, families and children.
Mrs Susan Porter – Parent Governor – term - 19/4/2026 – 18/4/2030
I am a parent governor at Shinfield St Mary’s Junior School, with one child currently at the school and another due to join soon. My professional background is in education, and I have taught locally for many years. I am currently a deputy headteacher and hope that my experience will support and strengthen the work of the governing body.
I am particularly passionate about high-quality, inclusive education and ensuring that every child is supported to thrive both academically and personally. I strongly believe in developing the whole child and in creating a positive environment where all pupils feel valued, confident and inspired to achieve their potential; working with parents to ensure this is successful.
Mrs Sam Lawless – Staff Governor term - 1/9/2022 - 31/8/2026
I am the staff governor and Deputy head of Shinfield St Mary’s and currently teach in the upper part of the school. I am honoured to have been a teacher for 26 years across 3 local schools and couldn’t imagine another job that I would cherish as much.
I have three children who are now 21,19 and13 who have been privileged to have been part of the Shinfield community and schools since they were 4. In some form, parent, PTA, teacher and governor I have been part of Shinfield St Mary’s since 2008. That’s a lot of School fetes!
In addition to my teaching role, I utilise my degree in religious studies to support the local RE community and represent teachers on The Standing Advisory Council for RE for Wokingham. This means I have been involved in developing our local syllabus as well as being invited to write plans to support these for the Oxford Diocese.
Nine years ago, I established an extra curriculum club to encourage girls to take part in football. This grew from strength to strength and I found I loved it so I am now co manager of a girls’ youth team for Shinfield Rangers.
Mrs Gill Morris - Lead Governor for Safeguarding and Allergies- Appointed by the Trust with the consent of the Oxford Diocese Board of Education – term – 28/1/2025 - 27/1/2029
Leavers in the last 12 months
Mrs Charlotte Parsons - Term 24/3/2025 - 15/7/2026
Mr Barrie Gilmour – Term 23/3/2026 – 15/7/2026

pageCache.pageTitle: Shinfield St Mary’s CE Junior School - SEND and Local Offer
pageCache.text:
SEND and Local Offer
Shinfield St Mary’s CE Junior School prides itself on being an inclusive, nurturing environment where all children can thrive. Love and inclusively is at the heart of our vision, ‘As I have loved you, so you must love one another.’ John 13, 34
We offer a graduated approach to Special Educational Needs, so there is a huge range of ways that we meet the needs of our children. We begin with a focus on Quality First Teaching with adaptions and differentiation to respond to the individual needs of all pupils within the mainstream classroom setting. We provide group or individual provisions as part of our 'Assess, Plan, Do, Review' cycle.
When needs are more complex and require increased support in a variety of areas, or the support of an external agency (such as: behaviour support, CAMHS, CYPIT) then a child could require a school ILP.
These ILP’s will be written, reviewed and shared with parents and carers at three points in the year:
Autumn Term – shared following Parents’ Evening one.
Spring Term – Shared following Parents’ Evening two.
Summer Term – Shared following the child’s report, moving with them to the next year group.
At our site we have a dedicated SEND classroom space, 'The Den' - where our Nurture sessions take place.
We are in the process of expanding our SEND resource, with a new playground classroom and nurture space within a recycled and repurposed double-decker bus!
Our SENDCo: Mrs Beth Webster
For all enquiries please use the email: senco@shinfield-st-marys.wokingham.sch.uk
Our SEND Governor is:
Mrs Charlotte Parsons: cparsons@shinfield-st-marys.wokingham.sch.uk

Our local offer can be found here - which provides details about what we offer at Shinfield St. Mary's Junior school
More information can also be found in our SEND Policy which can be found here

pageCache.pageTitle: Shinfield St Mary’s CE Junior School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Jesus said ‘As I have loved you, so you must love one another.’ John 13, 34
Our curriculum puts love of each other and the environment at the heart of everything we do, as reflected in our school vision. Positive relationships based on mutual trust and respect flow through our school and create a supportive and harmonious learning environment. Our ambitious curriculum is based on the National Curriculum, but adapted and enhanced with rich learning experiences, immersing children in progressive knowledge and skills. Ecology, sustainability and outdoor learning are pivotal to the enrichment of our curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Shinfield St Mary’s CE Junior School - Extra-Curricular Activities
pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular Activities
204 different children attended Extra-Curricular Sports Clubs (2022-23)
I went to my first club this year and I loved it! I learnt how to serve a shuttle in badminton. I can play with my mum now!
Each week, we provide a variety of clubs that are free to attend for all abilities and ages. We pride ourselves on providing ‘sport for all’, aiming to ensure that every child in the school attends one or more lunchtime or after-school club over the year. Your child is required to wear their normal PE kit for all after-school sports clubs. If the club is on the field, then they can bring boots, which are highly advised when the ground is uneven and slippery. Joggers and/or jumpers are, of course, allowed if the weather is bad. Please make sure your child has practised putting on boots, as staff have often found themselves tying up many pairs of laces, thus wasting valuable training time for everyone.
